text:
PagerBot: Alert — unusual KV cache growth in prefetch pipeline for region us-west-2. Threshold breach (cache_entries>1,000,000). paging: @oncall
Ram - oncall: I'm looking. seeing steady increase in KV entries, GC not keeping up. prefetched key fanout skyrocketed after yesterday's tokenizer shim deploy.
Maria L.: Confirmed. Loadgraphs: prefetch_worker queue length 120k, continuous-batcher latencies climbed from 30ms -> 450ms for mid-sized requests.
Samir: Any customer impact? CS seeing complaints?
Julie CS: A handful of customers on Dedicated noticed 5-10x tail latency and some request timeouts. No data exfiltration, but increased error budget burn and cost spikes for those tenants.
Ivy (eng-runtime): Logs show duplicated prefix keys — same logical prompt encoded into multiple token sequences. Suspect tokenizer change + hashing canonicalization mismatch. Hash outputs differ for templates with invisible whitespace.
Ram - oncall: Can we throttle prefetch and reduce batch size to stop the blowup? I can flip runtime flags.
Samir: Do it. Also disable prefetch + reduce continuous_batch_max = 8 -> 4. We'll also scale pool to absorb backlog.
Ram - oncall: Running:
```
# disable aggressive prefetch
curl -XPOST -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN" \
  https://ops.internal/api/flags \
  -d '{"PREFETCH_ENABLED":false, "CONTINUOUS_BATCH_MAX":4}'
```
Ram - oncall: Prefetch disabled, batch_max lowered, autoscale request submitted (x10 workers). Queue drain starting.
deploy-bot: Deploy 2026-03-14T23:42: small runtime config toggle applied to us-west-2.
Maria L.: Good, queue length falling. KV entries still high (900k) but not increasing.
Ivy (eng-runtime): Root cause analysis: tokenizer shim introduced a normalization that preserved zero-width joiners in some templates. Our prompt hashing function didn't normalize those, so identical logical prompts generated distinct cache keys -> prefetch produced redundant entries -> continuous batching matrix exploded.
Samir: Proposed mitigation path:
- Rollback tokenizer shim (short-term)
- Add stronger key canonicalization in hashing layer (mid-term)
- Add unit tests for zero-width characters and template whitespace (long-term)
Ram - oncall: Rolling tokenizer revert to canary 10% to validate.

```
git checkout -b hotfix/tokenizer-revert
# reverted tokenizer shim
git commit -am "revert: tokenizer normalization shim causing KV key divergence"
deploy canary -> us-west-2 worker-set-b
```
Ivy (eng-runtime): Also pushing patch to hashing:
```
# pseudo diff
- key = sha256(prefix_bytes)
+ key = sha256(normalize_whitespace(prefix_bytes).lower())
```
Samir: Tests and code review in progress. Estimated time to full rollout ~2 hours if canary stable.
Julie CS: CS notified affected customers with initial impact summary and mitigation steps. asking for ETA on resolution.
Ram - oncall: Handoff to Samir for ongoing watch. I'll be offline in ~30m. Samir, please page me if latencies > 2s or cache growth resumes.
Samir: Ack. I'm creating a follow-up incident doc and alert thresholds. Setting alert: kv_entries_growth_rate > 5%/min -> pager.
Ram - oncall: Leaving notes: PREFETCH_ENABLED=false, CONTINUOUS_BATCH_MAX=4, canary rev token-revert deployed to us-west-2 subset, autoscale x10 requested, CS updated.
Ivy (eng-runtime): Postmortem notes to include:
- Why normalization change wasn't covered by hashing contract
- Lack of end-to-end tests for template drifting/tokenizer interactions
- Add regression guard in canary gating (cache growth metrics)
Samir: Update: canary stable at 10% for 45m, KV growth flatlined, latency back to baseline for canary tenants. Proceeding with 50% rollout.
deploy-bot: Rolling out hotfix to 50%.
Julie CS: Customers acknowledged, appreciate the quick mitigation. No further escalations.
Samir: I'll own follow-up and write incident postmortem. Handoff complete to Samir (oncall) — feel free to ping in the morning for any stragglers.
Ram - oncall: Thanks team :thanks: handing off.
PagerBot: Incident closed to oncall handoff. next_check 30m.
